title: BuilderPublish
description: One Autopilot builder publish. The frontend emits this (gated); the composition creates the destination repository, optionally seeds it from a source repository, renders one git-provider LocalResource per file (committing the held bytes verbatim to a builder/<slug> branch on any SCM), and opens the change request. PER-PUBLISH fields (name/builder/branch/target/files/source) come from the claim; git/credentials/repository/pullRequest are INSTALL-LEVEL defaults (values.yaml) — the claim never carries a secret.

global.title: Global values
global.description: Helm global values passthrough. core-provider injects `global` into every composition's values before chart-inspector validates the render, so a root schema with additionalProperties:false MUST allow it — otherwise chart-inspector 500s and the composition never renders its LocalResource (issue #126). Every composition chart ships this.

name.description: Publish identity; LocalResource name prefix + krateo.io/publish label.

branch.description: Branch to commit onto, e.g. builder/my-dashboard (created off target.base).

target.description: The repo to publish into, within the install's git host.

base.description: base branch the builder branch is cut from.

files.description: The held files — each becomes one LocalResource (verbatim, at path).

path.description: Full in-repo path; the composition splits it into fileName + toRepo.path.

git.description: INSTALL-LEVEL git connection (values.yaml default). Not part of a claim.

scm.description: Which SCM this install targets. Selects the repository kind rendered by templates/repository.yaml; the file commits are scm-blind either way. Only "github" has a provider (github-provider-kog); any other value fails the render rather than skipping creation silently.

credentials.description: INSTALL-LEVEL git auth (values.yaml default). Not part of a claim.

username.description: Username for basic auth. Not a credential — GitHub authenticates on the token in the password position and ignores this value; it only has to be non-empty. Rendered into a chart-owned Secret (templates/username-secret.yaml). Ignored when usernameRef is set.

repository.description: INSTALL-LEVEL destination-repository policy (values.yaml default). Not part of a claim.

create.description: Create the destination repository as a CR. false = it is pre-provisioned; only the file commits render.

autoInit.description: Must stay true: without an initial commit the repo has no default branch and the file commits have nothing to clone from.

source.description: OPTIONAL source repository to seed the destination from, before the held files are committed. Rendered as a git-provider Repo (fromRepo -> toRepo). Omit or leave url empty for the previous behaviour: an auto-init'd repository and the held files on a branch cut from it.

url.description: Clone URL of the template repository, e.g. https://github.com/org/template.git. Empty = no seed.

branch.description: Branch in the SOURCE to copy from.

path.description: Subdirectory of the source to copy; the whole repository if unset.

intoBranch.description: Branch in the DESTINATION to seed. Defaults to target.base — seeding the base keeps the change-request diff to the authored files alone; point this at the builder branch to put the scaffold under review too.

krateoIgnorePath.description: Path to a .krateoignore in the source; the provider default is used if unset.

pullRequest.description: The change request, opened by the composition once every file is committed. Requires github-provider-kog >= 0.3.0 (the release that restores github.krateo.io/PullRequest natively); set create=false on older installs and open it from the portal's deep link instead.

create.description: Open the change request as a CR. false = stop at the pushed branch, the pre-1.9 behaviour.

body.description: Defaults to a line naming the builder, the file count and the claim.

filesBundle.description: The held files as a MAP of in-repo path to file contents — the shape a human can author in the portal, since the Form widget renders a property-less object as a JSON textarea. Equivalent to `files`; give one or the other. The composition emits the same LocalResource set, ordered by path.
